subject: TURN directive
notes: cite.py --check 7.3.25.4 "may be turned on only by specifying it explicitly within a TURN directive" OK. TURN half (probes via OPEN INPUT of a missing OPTIONAL file, status 05): TRNO1 EC-ALL ON -> not raised; TRNO2 EC-I-O ON -> not raised; TRNO3 EC-I-O-WARNING ON -> EC-I-O-WARNING; TRNO4 then EC-ALL OFF -> still raised; TRNO5 then EC-I-O OFF -> still raised; TRNO6 then EC-I-O-WARNING OFF -> not raised. PERFORM half: TRNQ1 'PERFORM OPEN INPUT F2 WHEN EC-I-O-WARNING ...' -> the WHEN runs with EC-I-O-WARNING; after END-PERFORM a second OPEN (status 05) does not raise it (status stays the EC-USER-X raised between); TRNQ2 WHEN EC-I-O and TRNQ3 WHEN EC-ALL do not enable it. All four halves verified. Test-ref empty: unit:TurnStateTests.EcAll_DoesNotEnableIoWarning witnesses only the TURN on/EC-ALL arm; the WHEN-phrase and end-of-PERFORM arms have no spec-derived witness. SIBLING DEFECT FOUND WHILE PROBING (not this rule's): a SUCCESSFUL READ with a nonzero status never calls the EC hook, so EC-I-O-WARNING is never raised by READ even when explicitly enabled — see findings (§9.1.13.1). || editions (adjudicator): 2023 (EC-I-O-WARNING and the exception-checking PERFORM are COBOL-2023 additions, Annex E)
